subject: Kestrel (P0) — tokens/sec & latency SLO mapping for Dedicated Fleet
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex@gokestrel.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec baseline and p95 target

Rachel —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We (Kestrel) are moving fast and procurement wants a clear dedicated sizing recommendation we can include in the MPA. High level: we expect steady-state API traffic for the first 12 months with the following profile: 70% short chat (avg 80 tokens/request), 25% assistant long-form (avg 600 tokens), 5% embeddings/rerank. Peak bursts expected during market opens (2x baseline) and product launches (up to 4x).

Immediate asks:
- An estimate of tokens/sec required for our projected baseline of 45k requests/day (mixed payloads above) and for 4x burst.
- Recommended GPU slab allocation (instance counts / model variant) to hit p95 latency < 450ms for chat, and < 900ms for long-form.
- A short list of risk items (quantization impact, KV cache warmup, seq length tail) and recommended headroom margin.

Can you send a quick sizing with assumptions this week? Procurement also asked for an XLS they can attach to the MPA — if you can drop that too, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Principal Product
KestrelAI
From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@gokestrel.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec baseline and p95 target

Alex —

Thanks — looping in Ben (capacity modeling) and Evelyn (SRE) so we can get concrete numbers.
Quick notes on approach so assumptions are explicit:
- We'll model two model variants: gpt-large-8q (quantized) for chat and gpt-large-16f (float) for long-form.
- Baseline mix translation into token/sec will use 45k req/day -> converted to 24h RPS and then per-second token throughput. We will present baseline and 4x burst.
- Latency SLOs are p95-based; we will target a 1.6x headroom over observed median behavior to account for tail and KV cold-warm transitions. If you want a more conservative 2.0x buffer we can show that as an alternate.

Ben — can you produce the XLS (capacity matrix) and include per-model tokens/sec, expected GPU utilization, and recommended slabs (GPUs + spare headroom) by EOD tomorrow? Evelyn — can you note any operational caveats (cache warmup, prefetch, live scaling limits) we should call out to procurement?

Thanks,
Rachel
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Alex Gomez <alex@gokestrel.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec baseline and p95 target

Rachel / Alex —

Attached is a concise capacity matrix (kestrel_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx) and the numbers below are the highlights and assumptions used. Please treat the XLS as the authoritative table for MPA insertion.
Assumptions:
- Workload: 45k req/day (steady). Mix: chat 70% (80 tokens avg), long-form 25% (600 tokens avg), embeddings 5% (1k tokens when used).
- Effective RPS baseline = 45,000 / 86,400 =~ 0.52 req/sec average; peak concurrent windows (daytime) we estimate 6x above average for short bursts; procurement asked conservative 4x for planning so we provide baseline and 4x scenarios.
- Model choices: 
  * chat: gpt-large-8q (8-bit quantized), avg tokens/sec per GPU = 6,800 tokens/sec (measured in our lab with 256 batch continuous batching, seq=96).
  * long-form: gpt-large-16f (float32), avg tokens/sec per GPU = 2,400 tokens/sec (seq avg=600, partial KV reuse).
- Latency breakdown target: p95 chat < 450ms -> we budget 300ms model, 150ms infra/queueing. For long-form p95 < 900ms we budget 650ms model, 250ms infra.

Sizing results (rounded):
- Baseline tokens/sec required (weighted):
  * Chat: 0.52 req/s * 0.70 * 80 tokens = 29.12 tokens/sec
  * Long-form: 0.52 * 0.25 * 600 = 78 tokens/sec
  * Embeddings (incidental): 0.52 * 0.05 * 1000 = 26 tokens/sec
  -> Total baseline ~= 133 tokens/sec
- 4x burst = 532 tokens/sec

GPU slab recommendation (targeting p95 SLOs with 1.8x headroom):
- Chat (gpt-large-8q): one A100-equivalent GPU yields 6,800 tokens/sec -> supports burst comfortably. For baseline a single GPU is overkill but required for headroom and failover. Recommendation: 1 GPU dedicated to chat with autoscaling to add 1 additional GPU at sustained >60% utilization or manual on-disk burst policy.
- Long-form (gpt-large-16f): one GPU yields 2,400 tokens/sec. With 1.8x headroom, effective capacity per GPU = 1,333 tokens/sec. To cover 4x burst requirement of 532 tokens/sec we need 1 GPU; to be conservative against tails and heavy long-form windows recommend 2 GPUs (primary + 50% spare) for region-local redundancy.
- Embeddings: route to hosted embedding pool (metered) initially; if Kestrel wants private isolation we recommend a small autoscale pool (1 GPU) with cold-start warmup mitigations.

Operational caveats / risk items (Evelyn please verify):
- Cold KV cache: first requests after deploy or significant model switch will see heavier latencies; recommend pre-warming during cutover windows.
- Quantization variance: gpt-large-8q measured quality delta ~0.8% BLEU-equivalent on Kestrel prompts; we can provide evals if they insist on float parity. Potential regressions during tail sequences >512 tokens.
- Burst headroom: if Kestrel expects extremely spiky traffic (20x), dedicated slab needs burst capacity in dedicated pool or fallback to hosted variants.

Deliverables included in XLS: per-model tokens/sec, expected utilization curves, recommended slab counts for baseline and 4x burst, and a short ops playbook for warmup and canary policies.

Next steps: Rachel to review language for MPA; Steph to produce a short bullet list for procurement about SLA exceptions and warmup timings.

-Ben
Principal Capacity Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@gokestrel.ai
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec baseline and p95 target

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying items before we move the XLS into our Docusign package:
- Can you note the committed monthly tokens and a suggested overage policy (we prefer an explicit overage rate rather than immediate throttling).
- For the MPA, procurement wants explicit SLA language: can Redwood commit to 99.5% uptime for dedicated slab and a remedy of service credits if p95 latency exceeds targets for 3 consecutive days? If you cannot commit, please propose acceptable alternative remedies.
- Also attach any security/compliance caveats we should surface (e.g., KMS integration, retention windows).

Alex will coordinate but flagged these as procurement blockers.
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: procurement@gokestrel.ai, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec baseline and p95 target

Hi procurement / Alex —

Quick answers and what we'll include in the MPA language: 
- Committed tokens: we will mirror the XLS baseline into a monthly committed token bucket (baseline * 30 days * conservative factor 1.15). Overage: standard per-token overage rate (0.0003 USD/token) during bursts until reserved capacity scales; we will provide a table in the XLS.
- SLA proposal for Dedicated slab: Redwood can offer an SLA of 99.5% uptime for Dedicated with an operational playbook; for p95 latency violations we propose the following remedy: if p95 exceeds the SLO for 3 consecutive days, Redwood will provide tiered credits (2% of monthly invoice per breach day, capped at 10%), plus a technical remediation plan and canary patch priority. If Kestrel requires a higher credit schedule, we can escalate to legal for negotiation.
- Security/compliance: attaching a short PDF redlines doc (kestrel_mpa_draft_redlines.pdf) that lists KMS integration (supported), log retention windows (configurable, default 30 days), and SOC2 evidence availability. Default data residency: us-west.

Operational suggestions: enable a warmup job during deploys to pre-populate KV caches (we can provide a small script), and schedule a controlled canary for the first 72 hours of go-live to monitor tail latency.

Next steps: Rachel — please confirm the XLS language for the MPA. Ben — if you can add the tokens->monthly commitment row and finalize the piecewise overage table we can hand this to Alex for signature.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
